nextGame.note: Saturday morning home game at Yulman Stadium, and it is Homecoming. Eleven o'clock our time. Tulane has won four games and lost four, and so has Tulsa.

news.headline: Tulane punter William Hudlow is up for a national award
news.summary: Hudlow is one of 65 players nominated for the Burlsworth Trophy, which goes to the best player who started college without a scholarship. He averages 47 yards a punt, the best in his conference.

news.headline: TJ Smith wins a conference award for his kickoff return
news.summary: The American Conference named Smith its special teams player of the week on Monday. He ran a kickoff back 95 yards for a touchdown at Charlotte with Tulane losing 10-7, the longest kickoff return by a Tulane player in two years.

news.headline: Tulane beats Charlotte 38-31 in overtime
news.summary: Tulane was behind by 10 points in the fourth quarter Friday night and tied the game with 10 seconds left. Dagan Bruno ran it in from the 1-yard line in overtime to win it, and the Green Wave are 4-4.

nextGame.note: Saturday night home game in Gainesville. A quarter to seven our time. Florida is 24th in the first playoff rankings. Oklahoma has won four games and lost four.

news.headline: Florida plans to start Tramell Jones at quarterback
news.summary: ESPN reported Thursday that Jones will start Saturday night against Oklahoma instead of Aaron Philo. Florida has not announced it, and Philo was pulled from the Georgia game after two interceptions.

news.headline: Florida suspends a starting defensive lineman
news.summary: The school said Wednesday that Jeramiah McCloud will sit out Saturday's game against Oklahoma, and gave his conduct as the reason. He has 22 tackles this season, and Florida will look at his case again after the game.

news.headline: Florida is 24th in the first playoff rankings
news.summary: The committee that picks the playoff teams put out its first rankings Tuesday night. Florida is 24th, and Oklahoma, the team the Gators play Saturday, is not in the top 25.

nextGame.note: Saturday morning road game in Columbia, Missouri. Eleven o'clock our time. Texas is 7th in the first playoff rankings. Missouri is 18th in those rankings and has won six games and lost two.

news.headline: Hollywood Smothers is out for the rest of the season
news.summary: Reports Thursday said the Texas running back tore a ligament in his knee and will not play again this year. He ran for 283 yards and two touchdowns, second most on the team.

news.headline: Colin Simmons may play Saturday at Missouri
news.summary: Texas listed its best defensive player as questionable on the conference injury report Wednesday night. He has missed the last two games with a sprained ankle, and the decision may not come until game time.

news.headline: Colin Simmons is up for a national award
news.summary: Texas said Wednesday that Simmons is one of 12 players still in the running for the Lombardi Award, which goes to the best lineman or linebacker in the country. He leads all of college football with ten and a half sacks even though he has missed the last two games hurt.

nextGame.note: Sunday home game in the Superdome against Cleveland. Noon our time, and it is this coming Sunday. The Saints had last weekend off. Cleveland lost 27-6 at Pittsburgh last Sunday and has won five games and lost three.

news.headline: Alvin Kamara is set to play Sunday
news.summary: Kamara practiced in full on Friday and the Saints gave him no injury designation for the Cleveland game, after he rested his back on Wednesday. Running back C.J. Donaldson is out with a shoulder injury and a concussion, and rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson is questionable for what would be his first NFL game.

news.headline: Cleveland rules out Deshaun Watson for Sunday
news.summary: Browns coach Todd Monken said Friday that his quarterback will not play in the Superdome because of a concussion. Rookie Shedeur Sanders will start against the Saints instead.

news.headline: Charlie Smyth will kick for the Saints on Sunday
news.summary: Coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that Smyth will handle the kicking against Cleveland. The Saints let their other kicker, Daniel Carlson, go on Tuesday.

news.headline: IUP's Jessica Neiman wins a conference weekly award
news.summary: The conference named Neiman its West Division athlete of the week on Monday. She had 32 kills in IUP's two wins last weekend, 17 against Pitt-Johnstown and 15 at California.

news.headline: IUP volleyball is second in its region
news.summary: The newest national numbers put IUP second in the Atlantic Region, behind only Gannon. Those numbers help decide who gets into the national tournament, and IUP hosts Gannon on Saturday.

news.headline: Peyton Belcher helps block three balls against Clarion
news.summary: Peyton played three of the four sets in Friday's win over Clarion and was in on three blocks. She had 3 kills on 14 swings with 4 errors.

news.headline: Cody Bellinger is up for a Silver Slugger Award
news.summary: Bellinger was named Thursday as one of nine American League outfielders in the running for the award that goes to the best hitter at each position. He was an All-Star this year and hit 17 home runs, and the winners are announced November 17.

news.headline: Cam Schlittler is a finalist for the Cy Young Award
news.summary: Schlittler won 14 games and lost 6, and no pitcher in the American League gave up fewer runs. The award for the league's best pitcher is handed out November 11.

news.headline: Yankees make a big offer to keep David Bednar
news.summary: The Yankees offered their closer a one-year deal worth $23.15 million on Monday, and he has until November 17 to take it or turn it down. They made no such offer to second baseman Jazz Chisholm, who can now sign with any team.

news.headline: Bonnabel beats Warren Easton 29-28
news.summary: The Eagles lost by one point at home Thursday night in the last game of their regular season. Warren Easton finishes the year 4-6, and the state playoff pairings are not out yet.

news.headline: John Ehret beats Warren Easton 35-18
news.summary: Warren Easton lost Thursday night in Marrero. It was the Eagles' first district loss and it ended a four-game winning streak, and it drops them from first place in the district to third.

news.headline: Warren Easton shuts out West Jefferson 44-0
news.summary: The Eagles won at home Saturday afternoon for their fourth win in a row. Warren Easton is 4-4 and has won all four of its district games.
